subject: Sovereign edge routing — on‑prem consequence matrix & acceptance
messages:
From: Cecilia Holm <cec.holm@atriabank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: Sovereign edge routing — network diagram + residency question

Hi team,

Thanks again for the call earlier. I’m attaching a simplified on‑prem topology for our EU and APAC sites (see atriabank-network-diagram-v1.pdf). A couple of concrete asks so we can close the security review:

- Confirm where active session state and KV cache would reside for a customer configured with EU primary, APAC warm standby. Will any tokens/temporary caches cross borders during failover?
- If we enable the proposed edge proxy in APAC (managed by us), what routing behaviors should we expect from Redwood’s control plane and runtime? Specifically, do any control messages, auth handoffs, or metrics payloads travel to non‑EU endpoints by default?
- We need a consequence matrix that maps outage scenarios to data egress risk (e.g., control-plane fallback to us‑hosted region, model variant switchover to hosted replica).

If you can send a short consequence matrix and a suggested acceptance checklist for our security/compliance team, we can move to procurement.

Attachments: atriabank-network-diagram-v1.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Cecilia Holm
Head of Infrastructure Security
AtriaBank

---
Note: AtriaBank security group CC'ed: security@atriabank.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sovereign edge routing — network diagram + residency question

Cecilia — thanks for the diagram and the clear asks. Attached is a first pass: residency-impact-matrix.xlsx. High level answers below, then a short acceptance checklist we recommend for SOC/Procurement.

High level:
- Runtime KV/cache: ephemeral KV cache for sessions is pinned to the serving cluster handling the request. With EU primary + APAC warm standby, active sessions served by EU clusters keep KV/cache in EU. During switchover we create a new serving session in APAC; the runtime will not replicate live KV cache across regions automatically.
- Control plane telemetry & auth: control plane metadata (job routing, version affinity) uses the customer control plane endpoint defined at onboarding. For Redwood Private VPC with the private control plane, control plane traffic stays inside the customer VPC (no egress to hosted control plane) — unless explicit failover policies route to Redwood-hosted fallbacks.
- Fallback behaviors: when capacity is exhausted in EU, options are: 1) fail closed (reject), 2) fail to EU standby nodes only, 3) fail to Redwood-hosted compatible model variant (requires explicit consent). The consequence matrix in the spreadsheet maps these to data residency/high‑risk flags.

Acceptance checklist (suggested):
- Customer signs explicit opt-in if Redwood-hosted fallback is permitted.
- Verify control plane endpoint is customer‑managed and peerable (no public egress).
- Confirm SNI/IP ranges for any monitoring/metrics ingestion endpoints (we provide a scoped list).
- Run a 2‑hour switchover test: simulate EU node failure and validate that no payload reaches non‑EU hosts unless opt-in fallback is active.

I’m attaching the matrix and a proposed canary config snippet.

Attachments: residency-impact-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), proposed-canary-config.yaml (txt)

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solution Security, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sovereign edge routing — network diagram + residency question

Cecilia — adding the technical consequence matrix context here (quoting your diagram above):

Scenario A — EU primary normal operation:
- Traffic ingress at EU edge -> routed to EU serving cluster. KV cache, transient logs, and debug traces remain in EU.
- Metrics/heartbeat: if customer exposes a private telemetry sink inside their VPC we post to that endpoint only. No default push to Redwood-hosted telemetry.

Scenario B — EU partial outage -> APAC warm standby activated:
- New requests directed to APAC standby cluster. Existing in‑flight sessions in EU are dropped (no cross‑region session migration).
- Control-plane reconciliation: orchestration will exchange minimal orchestration metadata (instance ids, routing decisions). We flag these as non‑PII; however if your compliance policy classifies orchestration metadata as sensitive, we can restrict reconciliation to within customer-managed control plane only.

Scenario C — EU capacity exhausted, opt‑in hosted fallback allowed:
- Model weights and inference execution move to Redwood-hosted replica (region flagged). Clear opt‑in required. Token payloads will transit to that region during fallback window—documented as high egress risk.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary: run traffic mirroring for 24 hours to APAC standby (mirrors only, no live sessions) to validate model parity and steady‑state egress behavior.
- Network: require mutual TLS and static IP allowlist for Redwood control plane endpoints.
- Audit: enable extended audit logs for the cutoff period.

Quoted for context: 
> On Fri, 10 Aug 2028, Cecilia Holm wrote:
> > ... If you can send a short consequence matrix and a suggested acceptance checklist ...

Let me know if you want this rendered as a short one‑page matrix for legal; I can produce that by EOD Monday.

—Soojin
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sovereign edge routing — network diagram + residency question

Team — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few leadership items to close the procurement path: 

1) Executive confirmation: Cecilia, can you confirm that AtriaBank will NOT permit Redwood-hosted fallback for production workloads unless explicitly enabled per deployment contract? We need that written to avoid accidental cross-border execution.

2) SLA carve outs: we can include a carve out that during regional catastrophes Redwood may execute emergency failover to a vetted Redwood-hosted replica only after a documented authorization process (signed emergency SOP). Do you prefer an on‑call approval or an automated HSM‑based escalation?

3) DocuSign & timeline: if the consequence matrix and the two acceptance checks in Rishi’s checklist are acceptable, we’ll route a limited‑scope Appendix (residency/fallback) for signature. I’ve created a preliminary DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/link/REDWOOD-ATRIA-APPENDIX-2028 (internal preview).

Please reply with: (a) yes/no on hosted fallback; (b) preferred emergency authorization flow; (c) target date for the 2‑hour switchover test.

Thanks — will align legal and infra once we have Cecilia’s confirmation.

—Jonas
VP, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sovereign edge routing — network diagram + residency question

Jonas / team — quick answers to unblock procurement: 

(a) Hosted fallback: NO for production by default. AtriaBank will only accept Redwood-hosted fallback in a documented, pre‑approved emergency SOP and after an explicit procurement opt‑in.
(b) Emergency authorization flow: prefer an HSM‑backed escalation token plus a 2‑operator human approval (one from AtriaBank security, one from Redwood on‑call).
(c) Switchover test: propose Thurs 2028‑09‑07 09:00–11:00 CET for the 2‑hour test. We will have security and infra on standby to validate logs and packet captures.

We’ve reviewed the residency-impact-matrix.xlsx — looks good. Please send the one‑page consequence matrix and the Appendix for signature; we will circulate internally and route to procurement.

Attachments: none

Thanks,
Cecilia
Head of Infrastructure Security, AtriaBank
